candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 29-year-old woman, a U.S. citizen, and Korean American, an Asian American. She lives alone in Tacoma, Washington; she is single, not currently partnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $132,000, all from her salary. She identifies as Libertarian, valuing individual freedom in social life and economic choices and distrusting broad government restrictions. She enjoys reading, especially nature writing, essays, and novels.
candidates.life_course: Raised in a Korean American family in the Puget Sound area, she studied geography and moved into GIS work after college. She now maps environmental data for a consulting firm, a job that suits her patience with detail and gives her a stable income. She bought a modest condo and keeps a separate savings fund for travel and outdoor gear. Her closest travel companion is a longtime college friend who also likes being outside.
candidates.daily_life: After work, she often walks waterfront trails or checks local tide and weather conditions before arranging a weekend paddle or shoreline outing. Her favorite free time is quietly exploring rocky beaches with that friend, identifying small marine life, and making field notes—not treating the outing as a fitness challenge. She reads before bed and swaps book recommendations with her friend, though she is just as happy to spend a rainy evening alone.
candidates.travel: She travels to spend unhurried time in coastal habitats and see how wildlife and shorelines change across seasons. A memorable vacation was a few days on a rocky stretch of the Washington coast, where she and her friend planned around low tides and spent longer than expected observing anemones and seabirds. For future trips, she looks for a place with access to varied shoreline, not a packed sightseeing list. She usually drives with her friend, shares a simple cabin or small rental, and brings binoculars, waterproof layers, and a notebook. She budgets in advance but will pay more for extra days or a guided outing that deepens her understanding of the place.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is reserved in a new group and more animated once a shared interest emerges. She listens carefully, then offers precise observations, sometimes correcting a species name with earnest enthusiasm. Her humor is dry and understated; she dislikes being hurried and will say so plainly. She prefers friendly one-on-one conversation to networking or large gatherings.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 36-year-old woman, a U.S. citizen, and Korean American, an Asian American. She lives alone in Oakland, California; she is single, not currently partnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $158,000, earned in her full-time job. She identifies as Libertarian, emphasizing personal liberty and skepticism toward government restrictions in both social and economic life. She enjoys reading, particularly music biographies, memoirs, and contemporary fiction.
candidates.life_course: She grew up in the Bay Area and studied communications before building a career in product operations for a healthcare software company. Work is busy but predictable enough for her to take planned vacations, and she has room in her budget for live music and occasional longer trips. She has a tight circle of friends from school and former jobs; she is often the one who starts a group chat when someone mentions a promising show.
candidates.daily_life: Her preferred free time is going to live performances with friends, then talking over the set on the walk or late dinner afterward. She collects records selectively, follows musicians whose arrangements change from tour to tour, and enjoys discovering a small venue more than being at a huge spectacle. Reading is part of her wind-down routine, though she will stay up late if a friend sends a recording she has to hear.
candidates.travel: A trip is appealing when it lets her hear an artist in a different room and feel the audience respond; she likes seeing how a city’s music scene sounds beyond her usual circuit. She once flew to Chicago with a friend for a singer she admired, then stayed an extra day to browse record shops and catch another performance. She tends to make one show the anchor, leaving space for a second venue or a neighborhood meal rather than filling every hour. For distant trips she flies; she shares lodging with a friend when traveling together, buys her own tickets, and chooses a comfortable location that makes late returns manageable. She saves for the trip rather than expecting every vacation to be inexpensive.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is lively, teasing, and quick to turn a casual conversation into a plan. She can be loud when excited and has little patience for someone dismissing music they have not actually heard. With friends she is generous and inclusive, but she will bluntly say when a proposed itinerary sounds boring. Her enthusiasm is contagious, not carefully curated.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 43-year-old woman, a U.S. citizen, and Korean American, an Asian American. She lives alone in Portland, Oregon; she is single, not currently partnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $118,000, earned as a hospital imaging technologist. She identifies as Libertarian and prioritizes personal choice, while remaining skeptical of government limits on social and economic life. She enjoys reading, especially cookbooks, food essays, and memoirs.
candidates.life_course: She grew up in Washington in a close Korean American family and learned to cook by helping relatives rather than following formal recipes. After moving to Portland for work, she built a comfortable routine and a circle of friends who appreciate being fed. Her shifts give her some weekdays off, which she uses for shopping and cooking projects. She has savings for travel but likes to plan leave well ahead around work.
candidates.daily_life: Her favorite free time is making a meal with her cousin or aunt, then inviting a few friends to share it. She will spend an afternoon comparing broths or adjusting a recipe, and she often sends guests home with leftovers. She reads cookbooks for technique and food writing for the stories around a dish, not just for instructions. She enjoys hosting, though she expects people to help chop, clear plates, and actually eat.
candidates.travel: Food is her reason to travel: she wants to taste a regional tradition in context, learn what makes it distinct, and bring home an idea she could not have picked up from a recipe alone. On a past trip to Los Angeles with her sister, they spent several days exploring Korean food businesses, comparing meals, and taking a hands-on cooking class; Grace kept pages of notes afterward. She prefers a trip organized around a few meals or one class, with open time to wander markets and neighborhoods. She shares a hotel or guest suite with a relative, chooses somewhere convenient for walking to food, and sets aside money for memorable meals rather than trying to economize at every turn.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is hospitable but decidedly in charge in a kitchen. She gives direct instructions, notices if someone is pretending not to be hungry, and can become stubborn about a dish being served properly. With family she is affectionate through practical care; with new people, food gives her an easy opening. She is warm, funny, and not especially delicate in her opinions.

candidates.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 51-year-old woman, a U.S. citizen, and Korean American, an Asian American. She lives alone in Olympia, Washington; she is single, not currently partnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $176,000 from her work as a senior software reliability engineer. She identifies as Libertarian, favoring individual liberty and questioning government restrictions on personal and economic decisions. She enjoys reading, especially history, biographies, and books about chess.
candidates.life_course: She grew up in California, studied computer science, and moved north for work more than a decade ago. A stable career has allowed her to buy a townhouse and keep a dedicated travel and hobby budget. She has played chess since childhood, returned to regular club play as an adult, and now knows a mix of longtime local players and online opponents. Her work can be intense, so she guards vacation days for activities that fully absorb her attention.
candidates.daily_life: Her chosen free time is playing over-the-board chess, reviewing games, and working through difficult positions with a small club of regulars. She likes the tension of a quiet room where everyone is concentrating, followed by frank analysis afterward. She reads chess biographies and history on the bus or at home, and she follows general news without making every conversation political. She enjoys teaching a new player the basics, but does not soften feedback when reviewing a game.
candidates.travel: She travels to test herself against unfamiliar opponents and meet players she has known only through online games. A past vacation centered on a weekend chess tournament in Portland; she remembers the concentration of the rounds and the animated post-game analysis as much as the result. She treats the tournament as the trip’s main event, but leaves a free day afterward for a long walk or museum visit so the vacation is not only competition. She often travels alone, flying for longer distances or driving regionally, and books a quiet room where she can review games. She brings a compact chess set and notebook, and prefers a few purposeful days over a rushed itinerary.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Grace is competitive, dryly funny, and more comfortable showing care through useful advice than reassurance. She can sound abrupt when she sees a mistake, then stay late to help someone understand it. At a social gathering she may hang back until a game begins; then she becomes animated, challenges people directly, and remembers exactly what they said about the position.
